To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the PRKAG2 Thr400Asn mutation causes early activation of AMPK, followed later by depression, that the AMPK activity in the heart correlates inversely with glycgen content, that TGT400N mouse hearts are susceptible to infarction after ischemia-reperfussion, and that the phenotype is partially rescued when the mice are crossed with a transgenic mouse that expresses a dominant-negative mutant of the AMP-activated protein alpha2 catalytic suibunit.
a mutation that increases AMPK activity causes glycogen storage cardiopyopathy and does not protect the heart against injury.
a mutation in the regulatory subunit of the AMPK complex leads to a biphasic activation of AMPK and that this mutation does not confer protection against ischemia-reprerfusion injury.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of a mutation that causes a glycogen storage disease in the heart.
the role of AMP-activated kinase in the regulation of energy balance and metabolism in the heart.
the role of AMPK in the heart, and the effect of mutations in the gamma subunit of AMPK on the heart.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a mutation in PRKAG2 causes biphasic AMPK activation and does not protect the myocardium from ischemia-reperfussion.

the TGT400T mutation in AMPK leads to a biphasic increase and then decrease in AMPK activity, which is responsible for the glycogen storage cardiopahy phenotype, and that despite this high glycogen content the heart is not protected from ischemic injury.
PRKAG2 mutations cause biphasic changes of AMPK activity in the mouse myocardium, and do not protect the heart from ischemia-reperfaction injury.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a dominant mutation in the regulatory subunit of the AMPK complex causes a glycogen storage cardiopathy.
the T400N mutation causes a biphasic increase in AMPK activity, which leads to excessive glycogen storage and cardiomyopathy.
a mutation in the PRKAG2 gene causes biphasic activation of myocardial alpha2AMPK, and does not protect the heart against myocardial ischemia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AMPK activity can be increased by a dominant negative mutation in the gamma regulatory subunit, but this does not protect the heart against infarction.
the T400N mutation in the gamma2 subunit of AMPK causes glycogen accumulation in the heart, and this accumulation is responsible for the phenotype of the mice.
the TGT400 mouse model of human PRKAG2 mutations has been developed and characterized, and that the TGT 400N mouse is not protected against cardiac ischemia-reperfussion.
